questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the core level of a product?

options.text: The physical features of the product.
The fundamental benefit the product provides.
The additional services offered with the product.
The brand name of the product.

questions.explanation: The core level of a product refers to the fundamental benefit it provides to the consumer, which is the primary reason for purchasing it.

distractorRationale.a: Option a is incorrect because it describes the actual product, not the core benefit.
distractorRationale.b: Option c refers to the augmented product, which includes additional services.
distractorRationale.c: Option d is incorrect as the brand name is part of the actual product, not the core.

questions.stem: Which type of consumer good requires the most effort in purchasing?
questions.explanation: Speciality goods require significant effort in purchasing due to their unique characteristics and the commitment involved in buying them.

distractorRationale.a: Option a is incorrect because convenience goods are purchased with minimal effort.
distractorRationale.b: Option b is wrong as shopping goods require some effort but not as much as speciality goods.
distractorRationale.c: Option d is incorrect because impulse goods are bought spontaneously without prior planning.

questions.stem: A product is always a physical item.
questions.explanation: This statement is false because a product can also be a service, which is intangible and provides value to consumers.

questions.stem: What is the actual product level of a laptop?

options.text: The brand and model of the laptop.
The ability to run software applications.

questions.explanation: The actual product level includes the tangible aspects of the laptop, such as its brand, design, and features.

distractorRationale.a: Option a is incorrect as the warranty is part of the augmented product.
distractorRationale.b: Option c describes the core product, which is the benefit of using the laptop.
distractorRationale.c: Option d is wrong because customer service is also an aspect of the augmented product.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of shopping goods?

options.text: They are compared on price and quality.
They require more time to make a purchase decision.
They are less convenient to buy.

questions.explanation: Shopping goods are not purchased frequently; they require more thought and comparison, unlike convenience goods, which are bought often.

distractorRationale.a: Option a is incorrect because shopping goods are indeed compared on price and quality.
distractorRationale.b: Option c is correct as shopping goods do require more time for decision-making.
distractorRationale.c: Option d is misleading; shopping goods can be less convenient but are not defined by this characteristic.
